mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5% over the next month reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the following 20-day period.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by more than 0.25% in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite FEDFUNDS increase, or the effect is statistically insignificant (p > 0.05 in a regression controlling for FEDFUNDS).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS crosses above 5%, it predicts a 5-day positive S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates further rate cuts.
failure_condition: No significant positive return in the next 5 days, or the cross is followed by persistent negative returns for 15 days.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly PAYEMS (employment) coinciding with a decline in UNRATE (unemployment) suggests strengthening labor market conditions that boost equity valuations and drive positive 20-day forward S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >2% while UNRATE decreases by >0.2% in the same month
failure_condition: No significant positive 20-day return when the labor/employment/unemployment interaction occurs as predicted.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in INDPRO (industrial production) by more than 2% signals weakening manufacturing activity, which lowers economic momentum and is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during INDPRO contractions.

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (retail sales) unexpectedly exceeds its 12-month trend by 5% in a given month, it indicates stronger consumer demand that is predictive of a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly surprise > +5% relative to 12-month trend
failure_condition: No significant positive return in the next 20 days despite the retail sales surprise.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising UNRATE (unemployment) above 4% signal labor market weakness that tends to depress equity valuations, resulting in negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises consecutively above 4% for two months
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE remains above 4% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both CPIAUCSL (inflation) and FEDFUNDS by at least 1% over the next quarter is expected to strengthen the real interest rate, producing a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL decreases by >1% while FEDFUNDS decreases by >1% in the next quarter
regime_hint: real rate strengthening via dual deflation
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive despite the predicted real rate increase.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent industrial capacity underutilization (INDPRO < 90 for two consecutive months), the S&P 500 exhibits negative 5-day forward returns as market anticipates a soft landing is less likely.
candidate_trigger: regime: two consecutive months of INDPRO < 90
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when the regime persists for three months.
